epics.description: Customers can export their paid orders as a CSV file from their account page. The export contains one row per order with order number, date and total amount including VAT, excludes cancelled orders, and is downloaded under the file name orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The delimiter and encoding of the file are not decided yet.

features.description: Customer capability to export paid orders as a CSV file from the account page.
features.name: Order export

acceptanceCriteria: Given a logged-in customer on the account page, When the customer starts the orders export, Then a CSV file is downloaded to the customer.
Given a CSV export is downloaded, When its name is checked, Then it matches the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.
stories.aiReadyReason: Which date the YYYY-MM-DD segment of the file name refers to, and which delimiter and encoding the file uses, are undecided, so a developer cannot make these product choices alone. Which date does the YYYY-MM-DD segment in the file name refer to, and should the file use a comma or semicolon delimiter with which encoding?
stories.description: A customer can start a CSV export of their paid orders from their account page and receive the file. The file name follows the pattern orders-YYYY-MM-DD.csv. The specification does not state which date the YYYY-MM-DD segment refers to. The delimiter (comma or semicolon) and the encoding of the file are not decided.
stories.iWant: to download my paid orders as a CSV file from my account page
stories.soThat: I can keep a record of my purchases
stories.title: Download paid orders CSV from account page

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with several paid orders, When the CSV export is generated, Then the file contains exactly one row per order.
Given an order in the export, When its row is read, Then the row contains the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT.
stories.aiReadyReason: The exported order date, the date and amount formats, the delimiter and the encoding are not defined, so the file content cannot be implemented without a PO answer. Which order date is exported, in which format are dates and amounts written, and which delimiter and encoding should the CSV use?
dependencies: Download paid orders CSV from account page
stories.description: The CSV file contains one row per order, with the order number, the order date and the total amount including VAT. The specification does not state which date is exported, nor the format of the date and amount. The delimiter and encoding are not decided.
stories.iWant: the export to contain one row per order with order number, date and total amount including VAT
stories.soThat: I can review my order history in a spreadsheet
stories.title: Export order number, date and VAT-inclusive total per order

acceptanceCriteria: Given a customer with one cancelled order and one non-cancelled paid order, When the CSV export is generated, Then the file contains a row for the non-cancelled order only.
Given a customer whose orders are all cancelled, When the CSV export is generated, Then the file contains no order row.
stories.aiReadyReason: The rule is clear and testable: cancelled orders are excluded from the customer's CSV export, with one row per remaining paid order and no rows when all are cancelled, so a developer can implement it as a filter on the export.
dependencies: Export order number, date and VAT-inclusive total per order
stories.description: Cancelled orders are not included in the CSV export. Only the other paid orders of the customer appear in the file, one row per order.
stories.iWant: cancelled orders to be left out of my export
stories.soThat: the file only lists orders that are still valid

tasks.description: In the backend code that gathers orders for the customer CSV export, exclude orders whose status is cancelled so that only the customer's other paid orders are selected. Expected result: the export data source returns one record per non-cancelled paid order and no record for cancelled orders.
tasks.title: Filter cancelled orders out of the CSV export query

tasks.description: Write automated tests covering both acceptance criteria: a customer with one cancelled and one non-cancelled paid order yields a CSV with a single row for the non-cancelled order; a customer whose orders are all cancelled yields a CSV with no order row. Expected result: both tests pass and fail if the cancelled-order filter is removed.
tasks.title: Add tests for the cancelled-order exclusion in the CSV export

stories.title: Exclude cancelled orders from export
